title: The circular flow of income
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:47Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point is a three-sector model with government, taxes and transfer payments taught at Victorian Units 1 and 2 depth, which is broader and more advanced than the two-sector household and business loop this Year 8 point needs.

draft.title: The circular flow of income
card: Households own labour, which is the work people do. They sell their labour to businesses.
Businesses pay households income, such as wages, for that work.
Households then spend that income on the goods and services that businesses sell.
That spending becomes money for businesses, which they can use to pay workers again. So money flows around the economy in a circle.
draft.remember: Households earn income from businesses, then spend it back on businesses.

a.q: Priya works at a bakery in Perth and uses her wages to buy shoes. What does this show about money?
opts: It flows from business to household and back to business
It flows from household to business and then stops
It moves only between households and never to businesses
It is spent once and does not return to any business
a.why: The bakery pays wages to Priya, and she spends them at a shoe business, so money moves from business to household and back to a business. It does not stop, because the shoe business can pay its own workers.
a.clue: Follow the money from the bakery to Priya to the shoe shop.

b.q: A large factory in Adelaide closes and its workers lose their jobs. What is a likely effect on local shops?
opts: Less income for households, so less spending at shops
More income for households, so more spending at shops
No change, as households do not spend their income
Shops gain money because workers stop selling labour
b.why: Without wages, households have less income to spend, so local shops are likely to sell less. Workers no longer selling labour means less income, not more.
b.clue: What happens to spending when wages stop?

a.best: It flows from business to household and back to business

b.best: Less income for households, so less spending at shops
